edits.old: Starting in MongoDB 6.1, the balancer distributes sharded data by collection data size rather than chunk count. The manual says a collection is balanced while its shard data-size difference is below three times the configured `chunkSize`; at the default 128 MB, a difference of 384 MB or more can trigger migration. Separately, Alibaba's ApsaraDB guide reports a trigger above 384 MB for its 128 MB default. Alibaba's support article scopes ApsaraDB's size-based policy to its MongoDB 6.0 minor 7.0.1 and later (mapped by Alibaba to community MongoDB 6.0.3); it lists minor 7.0.0 as chunk-count-based. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
edits.new: Starting in MongoDB 6.1, the balancer distributes sharded data by data size rather than number of chunks. The manual says a collection is balanced while its shard data-size difference is below three times the configured range size (chunkSize); at the default 128 MB, a difference of at least 384 MB is needed for a migration. Alibaba's ApsaraDB guide likewise reports a 384 MB trigger (three times the default chunk size) for MongoDB 6.0 instances, and notes that after upgrading to V6.0 (minor 7.0.1) or later, chunk counts may look unbalanced as expected behavior of the new balancer. Alibaba's separate troubleshooting page states the threshold behavior starts in MongoDB 6.0.3. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/release-notes/7.0/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/manage-the-apsaradb-for-mongodb-balancer ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/support/troubleshoot-mongodb-shard-data-imbalance

evidence.quote: Starting in MongoDB 6.1, data in sharded clusters is distributed based on data size rather than number of chunks.
For the default range size of `128MB`, two shards must have a data size difference for a given collection of at least `384MB` for a migration to occur.
If the size difference between two shards in a collection exceeds 384 MB (three times the default chunk size), it splits data by shard tag and migrates it using moveRange.
After you upgrade to V6.0 (minor 7.0.1) or later, sh.status() may show that chunk counts across shards are no longer balanced or that each shard holds a single chunk.
Starting in MongoDB 6.0.3, the balancer only migrates chunks when the data volume difference between shards for a given collection reaches a threshold.

edits.old: Configured chunkSize influences the maximum data amount the balancer attempts to move per migration, but it is not a hard size cap for stored chunks: MongoDB documents chunks that exceed the configured size when an indivisible range cannot be split. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Configured chunkSize affects the maximum amount of data the balancer attempts to migrate between two shards in a single chunk migration, but it is not a hard cap on stored chunk size: a sharded cluster only splits chunks when they must be migrated, so a chunk can exceed chunkSize (for example a 1 TB chunk with chunkSize 256 MB). Separately, MongoDB documents indivisible chunks (such as a range of a single shard key value) that cannot be split. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/clear-jumbo-flag/

evidence.quote: Maximum amount of data the balancer attempts to migrate between two shards in a single chunk migration operation.
A sharded cluster only splits chunks when chunks must be migrated. This means the chunk size may exceed `chunkSize`.
In some instances, MongoDB cannot split the no-longer `jumbo` chunk, such as a chunk with a range of single shard key value.
